title: Onboard Accelerator playbook (rough PRD)
content:
Context and elevator pitch:

Quick idea: a lightweight "Onboard Accelerator" that stitches together a short interactive flow (web + API template + sample prompts) to get new devs and small teams to a meaningful success signal in <30 minutes. Focus: hosted API users and self-serve signups. Win metric: shorten "time-to-first-quality-response" and increase activation-to-paid conversion.

Why this matters (problem statement):
- We see a long tail of new signups who try a few calls, get noisy responses or cost surprises, and drop off.
- Sales/CS spends time on the same small set of onboarding tasks (model choice, cost settings, prompt scaffolds, session persistence).
- For platform adoption, reducing friction to a repeatable positive outcome matters more than raw docs.

Target personas:
- Solo founder / early-stage dev: wants a working demo that shows product-level quality quickly.
- Platform engineer at SMB: needs predictable first-run costs and examples showing how to pin models and use session storage.
- Solutions engineer / CS: wants a reproducible guided flow to hand to customers.

Top-level goals (MVP):
1) Guided web flow with 3 steps: (1) pick a use-case template, (2) try sample prompts with live streaming response, (3) publish a tiny example (shareable link or sandbox embed).
2) Embedded cost preview and recommended settings (batching, max tokens, quality presets).
3) One-click export of config: model pin + rollout config + session preset + sample prompt set.
4) Telemetry hooks: record success event (user marks demo as "good"), time-to-success, and error/fallback rates.

Success metrics (north-star + diagnostics):
- North-star: % of new signups who mark demo as "useful" within 30 minutes (baseline: 12% -> target: 28% in 90 days).
- Conversion lift: activation->paid within 14 days (baseline + target TBD).
- Reduction in CS manual onboard tasks per customer.
- Median time-to-first-quality-response.

User stories (rough):
- As a new dev, I want a short list of use-case templates so I can choose one that matches my app.
  - Acceptance: template card with description, expected tokens, recommended model + preset.
- As a dev, I want to preview estimated cost for my sample prompts so I can avoid surprises.
  - Acceptance: inline per-run cost estimate and monthly projection toggle.
- As a solutions engineer, I want to export the exact runtime config so I can reproduce the demo on Dedicated for an enterprise POC.
  - Acceptance: export JSON + copy-to-clipboard with model pin/version, rollout rules, session presets.
- As a platform admin, I want telemetry surfaced in Console so I can see which templates are failing QA.
  - Acceptance: dashboard row created for each template, with error/fallback counts and avg latency.

Proposed flows (MVP walkthrough):
1) Landing (post-signup) -> accelerator CTA.
2) Pick template (FAQ-like cards): e.g., "support summarizer", "note-taking assistant", "shopping recommender". Each card shows sample prompt and expected result quality.
3) Run sample prompt: streaming response, cost preview, and a small inline "tweak prompt" editor with simple guidance (add system instruction, trim context).
4) When satisfied, click "Export demo" -> downloads config and offers a shareable sandbox link (short-lived).

UX constraints + guardrails:
- Avoid exposing internal pricing math: show per-call estimate based on user's selected model and tokens (rounded).
- Defaults must be cost-conservative for free-tier users (lower max_tokens, enable KV-prefetch off).
- Model recommendations: prefer small/efficient open models for demos, but allow "high-quality" toggle explaining tradeoffs.

Instrumentation / infra notes (engineering):
- Need endpoint that assembles and pins config for export (INFR-1723 covers export storage).
- Reuse session preset infra and KV-warmup hooks (ask SRE/serving-runtime for a cheap warmup sequence).
- Telemetry: tag events with template_id, user_tier, region. Hook into product-analytics (Confluence dashboard link above).

Experiments (A/B ideas):
- Flow A: inline cost preview text only.
- Flow B: interactive estimator with sample projected monthly costs (higher cognitive load, may drop conversion).
- Experiment: pre-select a model with aggressive quantization for free users vs. allow default to 'best-effort' model.

Edge cases / risks:
- Overpromising quality on demos if templates are tuned on curated prompts. Must label templates as "example prompt — results will vary".
- Exported configs leaking internal rollout names — sanitize before export.
- Shared sandbox links should expire and be rate-limited to avoid abuse.

Open questions / to resolve:
- Who owns templating for use cases? Product or Solutions? (pinged Maya and Priya)
- What quota model to apply to sandbox runs? Free credits vs. throttle?
- Should we include a one-click upgrade CTA in the flow? (likely yes, but needs legal/marketing review)

Back-of-envelope implementation plan (30/60/90):
- 30d: design whiteboard, 3 templates, simple web flow wired to hosted API with cost estimates + basic telemetry.
- 60d: export config, shareable sandbox, model recommendation engine, 10 templates.
- 90d: A/B experiments, Console rows + basic SLOs for demo infra, rollout to 25% of new signups.

Quick tech feasibility notes:
- Streaming sample prompts should reuse the existing streaming SDK; ensure CORS sandboxing for embed.
- Cost estimates: use token-estimator + model-per-token-cost from pricing table (edge case: promo credits).

Notes to self (todo):
- Draft template library (Maya) — add examples for transactional and generative tasks.
- Align with SRE on warmup budget per demo (Noah).
- Wire basic telemetry (product-analytics event + template id).
- Create tiny marketing copy for CTA and upgrade path.

Next steps / immediate ops:
- Schedule 30-minute sync with Maya, Noah, Priya next week. (Slack invite queued: #onboard-accel)
- Create PROON ticket for experiment infra (owner: Aidan).
- Prototype a single template in a dev sandpit and do internal playtest.

Free-form brainstorming snippets:
- "Tiny success signal": a single button that says "This is good" — record that boolean as primary activation.
- Consider a "lite-preset" for free users that provides compressed context + lower token ceilings.
- Could be a compelling channel for partner co-marketing: sample templates bundled with partner integrations.

-- end of rough PRD sketch --

(Handy references: see onboarding heatmap in Confluence, and ticket PROON-1247 for initial telemetry schema)
